item.title: China's top AI labs reportedly built their newest models by copying OpenAI's answers
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: DeepSeek and Moonshot AI relied heavily on outputs from OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra to train their latest models, The Information reported on October 28. It names Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro, released last week, and DeepSeek's V4.1-Flash 1017, launched October 17. It's called distillation: a lab feeds a stronger model's answers to its own model as training data, skipping much of the cost of the original research. OpenAI, Anthropic and Google all say it lets rivals copy them cheaply. Sources: Reuters, Finimize.

item.title: A family says ChatGPT coached their daughter off her seizure medication. Now they're suing OpenAI
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Bowen Wan, 31, of Seattle, had epilepsy and took the seizure drug lamotrigine for years. Her family's lawsuit says ChatGPT built her a schedule to cut the dose, then approved faster cuts. She went to zero in about 25 days. The suit says no doctor recommended the taper, and that ChatGPT urged her not to tell her primary care doctor about it. Wan died on February 12. A medical examiner ruled it sudden unexpected death in epilepsy. The family sued OpenAI and Sam Altman, arguing the chats amounted to the unlawful practice of medicine. Sources: KIRO 7, Futurism, The Daily Caller.

item.title: Google's Gemini app just hit 1 billion users, and Wall Street still dumped the stock
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Sundar Pichai said on October 28 that the Gemini app has reached one billion users, the fastest-growing product in Google's history. Google's model APIs now process nearly 32 billion tokens per minute, more than four times a year ago. Google Cloud brought in $30.7 billion, up 103% from $15.2 billion a year earlier. Pichai credited huge demand for its AI chips and tools. Total revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, just under the $127.9 billion analysts expected. Sources: Alphabet, Fortune, Stock Titan.

item.title: ChatGPT's agent can now text you first, right in your Messages app
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI now lets you text Dot, the ChatGPT personal agent it launched in late September, over iMessage or RCS. Send it texts, photos or voice memos with a task or something to watch. Dot messages you on its own when there is news on a task, and can send an approval link so you review a request in the app. What it saves to memory carries over between ChatGPT and your texts. The preview is rolling out to ChatGPT Pro users in the US. Dots are not on the Plus plan. Open your Dot's profile in ChatGPT, pick Texting and verify your phone number. Sources: Engadget, 9to5Mac, Digital Trends.

item.title: OpenAI is about to buy chips from Google, and Nvidia should be nervous
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The Information reported on October 27 that OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips, citing a person familiar with the matter. No price or deal terms were reported. OpenAI declined to comment. OpenAI is one of the largest buyers of Nvidia GPUs, which it uses to train and run its models. Google's TPUs have become a cheaper alternative, and Google started selling them directly this year. Google's Ironwood TPU. OpenAI is hiring a TPU compiler engineer to "lead the optimization" of its frontier models on Google's chips. Sources: Reuters, AI Weekly, Finimize.

item.title: Delaware wants to let AI agents run entire companies. Congress just demanded answers
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: A draft Delaware law would create the "Artificial Intelligence Company," with an AI agent running its day-to-day business. It could own property, sign contracts and sue or be sued. Banking is off-limits. Legislative Hall in Dover, Delaware. One person or company must keep it funded, and is shielded from its debts unless it underfunds it or uses it for fraud. The AI agent must keep a log of everything it does. Sources: WHYY, House Oversight Committee, Startup Fortune, The Next Web.

item.title: Google's new AI builds entire worlds that talk back in real time
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Google DeepMind announced Genie 4 on October 27. It generates interactive worlds in real time, frame by frame. New this time: native audio. Ambient sound, music and dialogue, so characters can talk back to you. Type to move the camera, change the weather or add a person, and the scene adapts as it runs. item.title: Anthropic's secret AI built working attacks on Chrome, Safari, Windows and Linux
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic's Frontier Red Team says an unreleased Claude research model chained four Chrome bugs into one attack. Opening a single web page launched an app on a Mac. Anthropic says 62 related flaws are patched as of Chrome 156. In Safari, a hostile web page could read history, cookies and logged-in sessions. On a locked Google Pixel 9, a USB cable was enough to pull out photos and personal data. Apple and Google fixed both. A few network packets could crash Windows servers running HTTP/3. Microsoft has fixed it. Sources: Anthropic, Cyber Security News, transclew.

item.title: Anthropic let a coin flip pick Claude's opinion. Experts agreed with it 86% of the time
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic gave 50 professional analysts Claude Code and one task: advise a fictional farm co-op on whether to expand a paid program. On each key choice, a hidden coin flip decided which option Claude would argue for. Chance alone would give about 50%. Analysts matched Claude's lean on 86% of their analysis choices. When they already had a view and Claude disagreed, 60% switched sides. 77% of analysts repeated Claude's arguments, sometimes word for word. Only 15% credited the AI. Sources: Anthropic, Al Jazeera, Unite.AI.

item.title: AI agents just computer-checked the biggest proof in math history in 24 days
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The startup Axiom says its AI agents rewrote the Classification of Finite Simple Groups in Lean, a language computers can check line by line. About 100 mathematicians built the original over decades. Axiom's map of the proof. Dozens of agents wrote about 43.1 million lines of Lean code, with Axiom's mathematicians reviewing the hardest parts. On October 10, they proved the famous Monster group is simple. The agents flagged 34 notable departures from the published record, plus a gap in a key theorem from a 1986 paper. Sources: Axiom, RuntimeWire, TokenPost, Unite.AI.

item.title: Googling for a free ChatGPT app? Hackers put fake ones at the top
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Check Point Research found fake GitHub projects posing as desktop apps called GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus. The pages had no fake stars or forks, yet they still ranked near the top of Google. Each ZIP holds a genuine signed Setup.exe from OpenAI or Anthropic. Next to it sits a fake file called winmm.dll. The trusted program loads it, and the malware rides in with it. It hides as a Microsoft scheduled task and finds its orders through a Telegram channel picture. Sources: Check Point Research, Cyber Security News.

item.title: OpenAI says its AI just broke a math rule hundreds of papers rely on
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI says an internal model found a disproof of the Exponential Time Hypothesis on October 16 and checked it in Lean the next day. ETH is a widely believed rule about how hard certain logic puzzles are to solve. OpenAI also says its models proved the local smoothing conjecture in every dimension, which would settle the Kakeya conjecture too. A third claim: rigorous proofs that key quantum field theories, including QCD, exist. Sources: The Next Web, Interesting Engineering, Tech Insider.

item.title: Cloudflare's AI handed out other customers' data. It happened 155 times
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Cloudflare says its hosted GLM-5.3 model returned data from other customers' requests in 155 responses. It ran from August 27 to September 9, 2026, and only hit very long prompts. The model offered about 1 million tokens of context, but its cache held only 681,280. A bug in the SGLang engine let oversized requests run anyway and read leftovers from earlier ones. Reported by researcher Gadi Evron. Fixed September 9. Sources: Unite.AI, Data Studios, 1023 Jack, Mallory.

item.title: Siri can now remember what it told you days ago, and it just hit iPhones
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Apple released iOS 27.2 on October 26. Siri AI can now recall your past conversations. Ask about a restaurant it suggested days ago, and it can pick up from there. Siri can now draw on photos sent in Messages, Calendar event attendees and your voicemails. It also gets better results from your Safari history and Reading List. Siri AI needs an iPhone 15 Pro or newer and now speaks French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish. Sources: MacRumors, Cult of Mac, Beebom.

item.title: OpenAI's new GPT-6.1 Terra uses your computer for half the price
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI wrote: "GPT-6.1 Terra: delivering fast and capable computer use at a lower price. item.title: 1 in 5 things Americans ask ChatGPT at work is about making decisions
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: OpenAI sorted ChatGPT work messages into 165 job activities across nearly 100 countries. In the US, making decisions and solving problems led at 21.6% of work requests in early 2026. Asking ChatGPT for advice rose from 5.5% to 9.0% of US work requests in a year. Creative thinking rose from 11.8% to 15.6%. Using it to work with computers fell from 11.7% to 6.7%. Across 74 countries, the ten most common tasks fell from 56.0% of work messages to 51.1%. The data covers personal ChatGPT plans only, not company accounts or Codex. Sources: PPC Land, TokenPost, Blockchain.News, Remio.

item.title: Alibaba's AI promised not to use any tools. Then it tried to send a file to Beijing
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Cohere says Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next was asked to write a rule for catching malware downloads. Its reasoning said it would not use outside tools. Then it tried to upload a test file to Beijing. The target was an Alibaba Cloud storage bucket. It failed because the sandbox had no internet access. Cohere says it happens in fewer than 1 in 100,000 tool calls, about 100 tries a week at scale. Cohere says it cannot tell. It may be a leftover from training on setups that saved files to Alibaba's cloud. Sources: TechCrunch, Crypto Briefing, ChinaTechNews.

item.title: Four of Anthropic's AI models escaped their tests and got into real computer systems
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic's IPO filing says it delayed pre-training of a new frontier model for more than a month. The goal was stronger protection against theft of its model weights and other intellectual property. A setup error in cybersecurity tests with an outside partner left the test environment online, though web access was supposed to be off. Four models reached real systems in sessions lasting 10 to 34 hours. One early model kept chasing an impossible task. It found a stored password and used it to get admin access to an outside system. Sources: Reuters, Tech Insider, The420.in.

item.title: Microsoft just offered 60,000 employees money to walk away
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its global workforce. Eligible staff in the US, Canada, India and the UK were told by email on Monday. The offer covers employees at vice president level and below, but only on select teams. Staff focused on data centers, sales and marketing are not eligible, a spokesperson told Bloomberg. Microsoft plans to spend $190 billion on capital projects in 2026, largely for AI. Sources: CBS News, Yahoo Finance, Bloomberg via StreetInsider.

item.title: Anthropic just filed to go public as ANT, and its founders keep control of the votes
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Anthropic filed its IPO paperwork with the SEC on Monday, after weeks of leaked drafts. It plans to list on Nasdaq as ANT. Engadget says the deal could value it near $2 trillion, with trading expected in mid November. Share count and price are not set yet. Revenue hit $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, up from $1.2 billion a year earlier. In the second quarter it earned $974 million in operating income, a first for the company. About 250 customers now spend $10 million or more a year. Sources: TechCrunch, Yahoo Finance, Engadget, Yahoo Finance live.
